text:
Six goals on 21 shots will end most arguments, and on Friday afternoon in Tampa it ended this one early. Ottawa beat the Lightning 6-2, and the gap between the score and the chances tells you most of what happened: the Senators had 2.78 expected goals (the quality of their chances, added up), and Dennis Hildeby allowed about 3.2 goals more than those shots deserved.

It started with a shot that almost never goes in. Ridly Greig scored on a 2% snap shot at 3:37 of the first, from Thomas Chabot. Tim Stützle added a shorthanded wrister at 12:47, set up by Michael Amadio. Ottawa then took over the second, 1.76 to 0.94 in expected goals: Amadio scored on a backhand at 6:20 with Claude Giroux and Greig assisting, and Stützle got his second at 17:37 on the best chance of the day for either team, a 44% look from Fabian Zetterlund and Dylan Cozens. That is a nice bounce back for Stützle, who left a game earlier this week after a collision with the goalpost.

The third period piled on. Artem Zub scored on another 2% chance at 6:17, and Giroux made it 6-0 at 7:55, with Amadio picking up his third point and Tyler Kleven, two nights after the Matthew Tkachuk hit that drew so much attention, adding an assist. Jake Guentzel spoiled the shutout with two goals, at 9:04 and 13:49, but by then the game was long decided. Linus Ullmark was steady, 18 saves on 20 shots and right at expected.

Our replays of every shot gave Ottawa the win 66% of the time. A deserved win, then, just not a 6-2 one. For Tampa Bay, the context is heavy: Conor Geekie is out four to five months after shoulder surgery, Pontus Holmberg is out a month per Daily Faceoff, and Nikita Kucherov's name keeps showing up in Montreal rumors. The Lightning took 25 penalty minutes to Ottawa's 11, and when the goaltending isn't there, a thinned lineup has nowhere to hide. Travis Green's Senators will happily take the afternoon off the power play, which, per their own game notes, has yet to score twice in a game this season.
headline: Senators score six on Hildeby in Tampa rout
